'''Nicholas Alexander Johnson''' (born December 22, 1992) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Saint-Quentin Basket-Ball|Saint-Quentin]] of the [[LNB Élite]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]], with whom he was named the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-12 Player of the Year]], and was then drafted 42nd overall by the [[Houston Rockets]] in the [[2014 NBA draft]].

==High school career==
Johnson attended [[Highland High School (Gilbert, Arizona)|Highland High School]] in [[Gilbert, Arizona]] from 2007 to 2009,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Tribune |first=Kyle Odegard |date=2011-12-29 |title=Former Highland star Nick Johnson's journey pays off |url=https://www.eastvalleytribune.com/varsityxtra/former-highland-star-nick-johnsons-journey-pays-off/article_68295a36-328c-11e1-8d19-0019bb2963f4.html |access-date=2025-09-10 |website=East Valley Tribune |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Obert |first=Richard |title=Nick Johnson returning to Highland to hold basketball camp |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/high-school/2015/06/23/nick-johnson-basketball-camp-highland/29173889/ |access-date=2025-09-10 |website=The Arizona Republic |language=en-US}}</ref> before transferring to [[Findlay Prep]] in [[Henderson, Nevada]] for his junior year. As a junior in 2009–10, he averaged 14.1 points, 4.6 rebounds and 3.4 assists per game as he led Findlay to a 32–2 record.<ref name=bio>{{cite web |url=http://www.arizonawildcats.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30700&ATCLID=207985400 |title=#13 Nick Johnson |work=ArizonaWildcats.com |access-date=July 22, 2014}}</ref>

In November 2010, he signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] to play college basketball at the [[University of Arizona]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.kvoa.com/news/arizona-recruit-chol-signs-letter-of-intent/ |title=Arizona recruit Chol signs Letter of Intent |work=KVOA.com |date=May 5, 2011 |access-date=July 22, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140729010405/http://www.kvoa.com/news/arizona-recruit-chol-signs-letter-of-intent/ |archive-date=July 29, 2014}}</ref>

As a senior in 2010–11, he averaged 24.8 points, 6.5 rebounds and 4.7 assists per game as he led Findlay to a 28–4 record. He was ranked as the No. 40 overall prospect in the country and the No. 8 shooting guard by Rivals.com to go with a scout grade of 96 by ESPN.com. He went on to be named a Long Beach Press-Telegram Best in the West first-team selection.<ref name="bio" />

==College career==
In his freshman season at [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], Johnson was named to the 2012 Pac-12 All-Freshman team. In 35 games, he averaged 8.9 points, 3.3 rebounds and 2.4 assists in 28.1 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name=stats>{{cite web |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/nick-johnson-1.html |title=Nick Johnson Stats |work=Sports-Reference.com |access-date=July 22, 2014}}</ref>

In his sophomore season, he earned honorable mention Pac-12 All-Defensive Team honors. At the Pac-12 Tournament in Las Vegas, he averaged a team-best 14.0 points to go with 4.0 assists and 2.0 rebounds per game. In 35 games, he averaged 11.5 points, 3.6 rebounds, 3.2 assists and 1.9 steals in 31.4 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" />

In his junior season, he earned first-team All-Pac-12 and Pac-12 All-Defensive team honors, as well as being named the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Player of the Year|Pac-12 Player of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web |title=2013-14 Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Honors |date=March 10, 2014 |work=Pac-12.com |url=https://pac-12.com/news/2014/3/10/2013-14-pac-12-conference-mens-basketball-honors.aspx |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140312033514/http://pac-12.com/article/2014/03/10/2013-14-pac-12-conference-mens-basketball-honors |archive-date=March 12, 2014 |url-status=live |access-date=March 11, 2014}}</ref> He finished his career ranked 24th on UA's scoring list with 1,333 points. In 38 games, he averaged 16.3 points, 4.1 rebounds, 2.8 assists and 1.1 steals in 33.1 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" /><ref name="stats" />

On April 15, 2014, he declared for the NBA draft, foregoing his final year of college eligibility.<ref>{{cite web |last=Norlander |first=Matt |url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/24527989/arizonas-aaron-gordon-and-nick-johnson-leaving-for-nba-draft |title=Arizona's Aaron Gordon and Nick Johnson leaving for NBA Draft |work=CBSSports.com |date=April 15, 2014 |access-date=July 22, 2014}}</ref>

==Professional career==
===Houston Rockets (2014–2015)===
On June 26, 2014, Johnson was selected with the 42nd overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Steinberg |first=Russell |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2014/6/26/5848208/nick-johnson-houston-rockets-nba-draft-results-2014 |title=2014 NBA Draft Results: Houston Rockets select Nick Johnson with 42nd pick |work=SBNation.com |date=June 26, 2014 |access-date=July 22, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Friedman |first=Jason |url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/rockets-introduce-capela-and-johnson |title=Rockets Introduce Capela and Johnson |work=NBA.com |date=June 30, 2014 |access-date=July 22, 2014}}</ref> On July 25, 2014, he signed with the Rockets after averaging 12.5 points per game during the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.khou.com/story/sports/2014/07/29/12678154/ |title=Rockets officially sign draft picks Capela, Johnson |work=KHOU.com |date=July 25, 2014 |access-date=July 25, 2014 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20140821122630/http://www.khou.com/story/sports/2014/07/29/12678154/ |archive-date=August 21, 2014 |url-status=dead}}</ref> During his rookie season, he received multiple assignments to the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite news |title=All-Time NBA Assignments |url=http://dleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/ |access-date=December 11, 2015 |work=NBA.com |archive-date=March 22, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170322122733/http://dleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

On July 20, 2015, the Rockets traded Johnson, [[Joey Dorsey]], [[Kostas Papanikolaou]], [[Pablo Prigioni]], a [[2016 NBA draft|2016 first-round draft]] pick, and cash considerations to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in exchange for [[Ty Lawson]] and a [[2017 NBA draft|2017 second-round draft]] pick.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-acquire-joey-dorsey-nick-johnson-kostas-papanikolaou-pablo-prigioni-cash-considerations |title=Nuggets Acquire Joey Dorsey, Nick Johnson, Kostas Papanikolaou, Pablo Prigioni, Cash Considerations and First Round Pick From Houston |work=NBA.com |date=July 20, 2015 |access-date=July 20, 2015}}</ref> On October 24, 2015, he was waived by the Nuggets after appearing in six preseason games.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=18518 |title=Nuggets waive Nick Johnson, Oleksiy Pecherov, Devin Sweetney |work=InsideHoops.com |date=October 24, 2015 |access-date=October 24, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160113060306/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=18518 |archive-date=January 13, 2016 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Austin Spurs (2015–2016)===
On December 28, 2015, Johnson was acquired by the [[Austin Spurs]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://austin.dleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-acquire-nick-johnson/ |title=Austin Spurs Acquire Nick Johnson |work=NBA.com |date=December 28, 2015 |access-date=December 28, 2015 |archive-date=December 30, 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151230224942/http://austin.dleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-acquire-nick-johnson/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> In 34 games for Austin in 2015–16, he averaged 10.4 points, 3.7 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.0 steals per game.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/dleague/players/j/johnsni02d.html |title=Nick Johnson D-League Stats |work=Basketball-Reference.com |access-date=October 22, 2016}}</ref>

On September 8, 2016, Johnson signed with the [[Orlando Magic]],<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-sign-six-free-agents-training-camp-nick-johnson-cliff-alexander-damjan-rudez-20160908 |title=Orlando Magic Sign Six Players |work=NBA.com |date=September 8, 2016 |access-date=September 8, 2016}}</ref> but was waived on October 22 after appearing in four preseason games.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/orlando-magic-waive-nick-johnson-ramon-galloway |title=Orlando Magic Waive Nick Johnson, Ramon Galloway |work=NBA.com |date=October 22, 2016 |access-date=October 22, 2016}}</ref>

===Bayern Munich (2016–2017)===
On October 29, 2016, Johnson signed with [[FC Bayern Munich (basketball)|Bayern Munich]] of the German [[Basketball Bundesliga]] till the end of the season.<ref>{{cite news |title=Bayern Munich signs Nick Johnson |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/215799/bayern-munich-signs-nick-johnson.html |work=Sportando.com |date=October 29, 2016 |access-date=October 29, 2016}}</ref>

===Second Stint with Austin Spurs (2017–2019)===
On November 2, 2017, Johnson was included in the 2017–18 opening night roster for [[Austin Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Opening Night Roster |url=https://twitter.com/austin_spurs/status/926220077795561472 |website=Twitter.com |access-date=November 2, 2017 |date=November 2, 2017}}</ref> He helped the [[Austin Spurs]] win the [[G League championship]] and was named the [[G League Finals MVP]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://gleague.nba.com/games/20180410ausrap/ |title=Spurs Win NBA G League Championship, Defeat Raptors 905 in Game 2 |work=NBA.com |date=April 10, 2018 |access-date=April 10, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |first1=Alex |last1=Busch |url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/nick-johnsons-finals-mvp-award-just-performance/ |title=Nick Johnson's Finals MVP Award About More Than Just Performance |work=NBA.com |date=April 11, 2018 |access-date=April 11, 2018}}</ref>

He was signed by the [[San Antonio Spurs]] and played four preseason games before being waived.<ref>{{cite news |last=Garcia |first=Jeff |title=Spurs waive Nick Johnson, Okaro White |date=October 14, 2018 |website=News4SanAntonio.com |url=https://news4sanantonio.com/sports/spurs-zone/spurs-waive-nick-johnson-okaro-white |access-date=November 19, 2018}}</ref> On November 18, 2018, he was reacquired by the Austin Spurs.<ref>{{cite press release |title=Austin Spurs Acquire Nick Johnson |date=November 18, 2018 |publisher=Austin Spurs |url=https://austin.gleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-acquire-nick-johnson-2/ |access-date=November 19, 2018}}</ref>

===Wisconsin Herd (2019)===
On January 16, 2019, Johnson was acquired by the [[Wisconsin Herd]] with returning right of [[Olivier Hanlan]] and a second-round pick in the [[2019 NBA G League Draft]] for [[Travis Trice]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Wisconsin Herd Acquires Nick Johnson in Trade with Austin Spurs |url=https://wisconsin.gleague.nba.com/news/wisconsin-herd-acquires-nick-johnson-in-trade-with-austin-spurs/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 16, 2019 |date=January 16, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Austin Spurs Obtain Travis Trice in Trade with Wisconsin Herd |url=https://austin.gleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-obtain-travis-trice-in-trade-with-wisconsin-herd/ |website=NBA.com |access-date=January 16, 2019 |date=January 16, 2019 |archive-date=January 17, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190117021915/https://austin.gleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-obtain-travis-trice-in-trade-with-wisconsin-herd/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Nanterre 92 (2019)===
On March 22, 2019, Johnson signed with [[Nanterre 92]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Nanterre adds Nick Johnson to replace injured Dominic Waters |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/proa/848868/nanterre-adds-nick-johnson-to-replace-injured-dominic-waters/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=April 11, 2019 |date=March 22, 2019}}</ref>

===Türk Telekom (2019–2021)===
On September 5, 2019, he signed with [[Türk Telekom B.K.|Türk Telekom]] of [[Turkish Basketball Super League|Turkish Super League]].<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/turk-telekom-signs-nick-johnson/ |title=Turk Telekom signs Nick Johnson |date=September 5, 2019 |newspaper=Sportando |language=En |access-date=September 5, 2019 |last1=Maggi |first1=Alessandro }}</ref> Johnson averaged 11.6 points, 3.7 rebounds and 4.3 assists per game. He re-signed with the team on October 27, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Nick Johnson returns to Turk Telekom Ankara |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/nick-johnson-returns-to-turk-telekom-ankara/ |website=Sportando |access-date=October 27, 2020 |date=October 27, 2020 |last1=Lupo |first1=Nicola }}</ref>

===Second Stint with Nanterre 92 (2021–2022)===
On July 30, 2021, he has signed with [[Nanterre 92]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/nick-johnson-is-back-in-nanterre/|title=Nick Johnson is back in Nanterre|last=|first=|date=July 30, 2021|website=|newspaper=Sportando|language=En|access-date=August 1, 2021 |last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano }}</ref>

===Hapoel Holon (2023)===
On November 6, 2023, he signed with [[Hapoel Holon B.C.|Hapoel Holon]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/nick-johnson-joins-hapoel-holon/|title=Nick Johnson joins Hapoel Holon|last=|first=|date=November 6, 2023|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=November 9, 2023}}</ref>

===Trefl Sopot (2024–2025)===
On November 27, 2024, he signed with [[Trefl Sopot]] in the [[Polish Basketball League]] (PLK).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://plk.pl/aktualnosci/25152/nick-johnson-dolacza-do-trefla|title=Nick Johnson dołącza do Trefla|last=|first=|date=November 27, 2024|website=plk.pl|publisher=|language=pl|access-date=December 2, 2024}}</ref>

===Saint-Quentin (2025–present)===
On July 25, 2025, he signed with [[Saint-Quentin Basket-Ball|Saint-Quentin]] of the [[LNB Pro A]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://sqbb.fr/actualites/article/1229|title=Nick Johnson Est Un Phénix|date=July 25, 2025|website=sqbb.fr|publisher=|language=fr|access-date=October 11, 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Johnson's father, Joey, and his uncle, [[Dennis Johnson|Dennis]], are both former professional basketball players with the latter being a three-time NBA champion and a member of the [[Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Coro |first=Paul |url=https://www.azcentral.com/sports/ua/articles/2011/12/11/20111211arizona-wildcats-basketball-freshman-nick-johnson.html |title=Arizona Wildcats freshman Nick Johnson already maturing |work=AZCentral.com |date=December 11, 2011 |access-date=July 22, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Branch |first=John |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2014/03/21/sports/ncaabasketball/a-fathers-legs-and-an-uncles-skills.html |title=A Father's Legs and an Uncle's Skills |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=March 20, 2014 |access-date=July 22, 2014}}</ref>
